title: Paloma and the Garden
premise: Beatrix Ravensworth, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent her life guarding the smuggler roads of the Thornfell mountains, hiding from a prophecy she never wanted to be part of. When her date, cartographer Paloma Idris, arrives carrying an antique book that names them both — and tonight's date — they are pulled bodily into a century-old prophecy still unfolding beneath Thornfell's crown. To free King Aldric from the crown-spirit that has worn him for generations, Beatrix must reclaim the swordspeaking oath she abandoned and Paloma must map a garden that exists only in memory. They succeed at terrible cost: the king dies freed, the prophecy closes, and Beatrix and Paloma choose each other freely, unbound by fate.
about_author: Tamsin Vasquez is a former trail guide who writes fantasy rooted in mountain folklore and found family. She lives in a converted fire lookout with two opinionated goats and an ever-growing collection of hand-drawn maps.

chapters.title: The Date
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix meets Paloma at a Thornfell waystation tavern for a carefully arranged first date, both nervous behind their competence. A cartographer and a smuggler's guide make odd company, but the spark is real. Emotional beat: guarded hope interrupted when Paloma produces a strange old book as a gift.

chapters.title: Ink That Knows Your Name
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma explains she bought the book to impress Beatrix — a century-old prophecy of the Ravensworth line. The ink shifts as they read, naming tonight's date, this tavern, this hour. The candle gutters; the room folds inward like a closing map. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as the book pulls them under.

chapters.title: A Century Deep
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. They wake on a mountain road that shouldn't exist, under stars arranged wrong, in the year the prophecy was written. Beatrix recognizes the landscape from her grandmother's stories — the Thornfell before the fall. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into resolve as Beatrix realizes her family's oaths began here.

chapters.title: The Garden Below
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Following the book's verses, they find a hidden valley garden blooming out of season, tended by no one, where every plant grows from a buried memory. Paloma's maps begin redrawing themselves in her satchel. Emotional beat: awe and unease — the garden responds to Paloma as if it knows her.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In the valley's edge village they learn King Aldric still reigns here, young and wrong-eyed, his shadow moving a half-second behind him. A dying hedge-witch tells them the crown is not an object but a tenant. Emotional beat: dread — Beatrix understands the prophecy's true villain.

chapters.title: Oathbound
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The hedge-witch recognizes the Ravensworth sword-marks on Beatrix's hands and demands she speak the old oath aloud. Beatrix refuses — the oath cost her mother everything — but the sword at her hip answers anyway, waking. Emotional beat: guilt and resistance against an inheritance she never chose.

chapters.title: Cartography of the Impossible
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma discovers her own ancestor drew the original garden maps and vanished into them; the book chose her bloodline too. She begins mapping the garden properly, learning its rules: it grows toward truths people refuse to say. Emotional beat: purpose — Paloma claims her own inheritance.

chapters.title: The King's Hunt
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Crown soldiers sweep the valley hunting 'the two named in the verse.' Beatrix leads Paloma through smuggler routes that exist only in her memory of stories, proving her worth beyond the sword. Emotional beat: confidence rebuilding — her knowledge matters as much as any oath.

chapters.title: Audience with a Hollow Man
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Captured deliberately, they are brought before King Aldric, who briefly surfaces inside himself to beg them — in a child's handwriting scrawled on his own palm — to end it. The crown-spirit watches through his eyes. Emotional beat: horror laced with compassion for the man inside the monster.

chapters.title: Escape by Old Roads
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A daring escape through the palace's forgotten ways, guided by Beatrix's grandmother's smuggler rhymes sung under her breath. They lose the sword but gain an ally: Aldric's sworn shield, Serah, who has suspected the truth for years. Emotional beat: hard-won trust and grief for what the king once was.

chapters.title: Serah's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. In hiding, Serah recounts the crown's history: every monarch it wears grows kinder in public and emptier in private, until nothing remains. The spirit feeds on identity itself. Paloma realizes the garden's memory-plants are the crown's discarded meals. Emotional beat: the stakes become personal and existential.

chapters.title: The Verse That Wasn't Written
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Studying the book, Beatrix finds a final verse smudged beyond reading — deliberately censored by a previous Ravensworth. Her grandmother's letters hint the last swordspeaker tried to break the oath instead of keep it, and failed catastrophically. Emotional beat: foreboding about the price of defiance.

chapters.title: Roots and Reckonings
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The garden offers Paloma a memory-plant grown from Beatrix's buried past: the night Beatrix renounced her oath and let her sister walk into danger alone. Paloma must decide whether truth or tenderness serves them better. Emotional beat: intimacy tested by painful honesty.

chapters.title: The Fight Beneath the Trellis
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Confronted with the memory, Beatrix breaks — then rages — then finally speaks the whole truth aloud, and the garden blooms wildly around her, the oath settling into her like roots rather than chains. Emotional beat: catharsis; acceptance transforms inheritance into choice.

chapters.title: March on the Pale Court
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. With Serah's help, the three plan the assault: Paloma will map the crown's true name in the garden, Beatrix will speak it unbound, Serah will hold the door. The book's pages begin burning from the back forward — time is literally running out. Emotional beat: grim determination against a deadline.

chapters.title: The Burning Book
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. As the prophecy consumes itself, the crown-spirit strikes early, flooding the valley with soldiers wearing the faces of people its victims loved. Beatrix holds the pass alone, speaking her oath for the first time in battle. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce, joyful power.

chapters.title: The Garden's True Name
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. In the garden's heart, Paloma completes the impossible map and reads the crown-spirit's origin: it was once a gardener-king who refused to die and ate his successors' selves to persist. Emotional beat: pity for the monster — it began as a man afraid of ending.

chapters.title: Throne of Thorns
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Climax begins: Beatrix and Paloma breach the throne room, Serah falling wounded to buy them seconds. Beatrix speaks the crown's true name while Paloma anchors her to the present with the map. The spirit tears at Beatrix's identity, offering her everything she's ever wanted to belong. Emotional beat: peak peril, identity under siege.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma reaches Aldric through the spirit's grip by showing him his own palm-scrawl — his last honest act — and he chooses, finally, to let go. Beatrix's spoken name unravels the crown; the spirit dissolves into the garden it starved. Emotional beat: release, grief, and grace entwined.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Verse
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The freed kingdom begins remembering itself, but Aldric does not survive the unbinding; Serah lives, changed. The book burns to ash in Beatrix's hands, the prophecy complete. Beatrix fears the oath died with it — until the sword hums, hers now by choice. Emotional beat: mourning braided with quiet triumph.

chapters.title: Two Roads Home
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Standing at the fold between centuries, Paloma and Beatrix realize the pull is gone — whatever happens next is unwritten. They choose to return together, carrying seeds from the garden and Serah's promise to rebuild. Emotional beat: love affirmed without destiny's excuse.

chapters.title: Paloma and the Garden
chapters.summary: POV Both, alternating. Back in the present, they replant the garden's seeds above Thornfell, where they grow ordinary and stubborn and theirs. Beatrix trains new swordspeakers by invitation, not oath; Paloma publishes maps no prophecy dictated. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, identity inherited and remade — a quiet, earned happy ending.
